pages.bodyText: Skip to content Vitalii Oborskyi Home Research Writing Talks Appearance Display follows your browser’s color preference. Animated motion needs JavaScript. AI delivery governance & agentic operating models Vitalii Oborskyi . AI tools everywhere. Better delivery? Harder to tell. I help software organizations investigate why AI adoption is not improving delivery, rebalance review and ownership, and define controls for agentic systems in production. For enterprise software teams and IT services companies. Discuss your AI challenge Explore the research AI is a fundamental shift: an attempt to delegate parts of thinking to machines. I study what that changes in software delivery and the systems we design. My work draws on more than 20 years across quality engineering, project management, PMO and delivery leadership. Research Writing Work with me 01 / Research Two questions behind the work. What happens when machines generate faster than people can understand and verify? And what changes when the software itself relies on model judgment? 01 / How we build How do we rebalance AI-assisted delivery? I see the AI-assisted SDLC as structurally unbalanced where generation accelerates faster than human understanding, verification and ownership. More output can coexist with review queues, rework and fragile maintenance. The Subprime Code Crisis investigates this gap and what it would take to rebalance the work. My working position is that existing playbooks do not yet offer a generally validated recipe for resolving it. Explore delivery research ↗ Methods & evidence ↗ Start with Externalization & the verification crisis . 02 / What we build and operate How do we engineer systems that rely on model judgment? Uncertainty Architecture studies what I call Thinking Systems: software in which consequential runtime responsibilities depend partly on probabilistic model judgment. This is where I see the fullest expression of today's AI potential — and some of its hardest engineering problems. The engineering object includes people, evidence, authority and correction mechanisms, alongside software. It needs development lifecycles and operating models suited to uncertainty. Much remains to develop and test. Explore systems research ↗ Living specification ↗ Start with Thinking Systems . 02 / Where I can help Start with the decision you need to make. Delivery / Diagnosis “We bought AI tools. Delivery is not improving.” Assess the delivery flow, review and verification capacity, rework, knowledge dependencies and costs. Investigate the actual constraint. Possible output: a problem/risk map and prioritized experiments or changes to test. Architecture / Runtime governance “The demo works. Production is hard to control.” Review delegated judgment, permissions, limits, evaluation evidence, cost ownership, escalation and corrective action. Possible output: a control/ownership sketch and explicit unresolved release questions. SDLC / QA / Operating model “Our process and roles have not caught up with AI.” Work through requirements, evaluation, release decisions and human capacity in a focused workshop. Possible output: draft role and decision boundaries, learning routines and an improvement backlog. The first conversation determines fit and scope; outputs depend on the agreed engagement. Discuss your AI challenge → 03 / Selected writing Five ways into the work. Thinking Systems for architecture; Externalization for generation and verification; Moat for strategic differentiation. All five selected editions are English. 30 Aug 2026 EN · English · Article · Generative AI Uncertainty Architecture: Thinking Systems, When the Controlled Object Changes LinkedIn edition · 27 Aug 2026 What changes when consequential runtime responsibility depends on model judgment. 12 Jun 2026 EN · English · Article · Agile Insider AI, the Externalization of Reasoning, and the Verification Crisis Why faster generation raises questions of human understanding and verification. 10 Jun 2026 EN · English · Article · LinkedIn Reinventing Control Theory One Feature at a Time: The Fallacy of Agentic Loops A control-theory perspective on agentic loops and engineering control. 10 Jun 2026 EN · English · Article · Generative AI Uncertainty Architecture: Beyond Embeddings — Neuro-Symbolic Verification of Semantic Drift in LLMs A bounded technical example of semantic verification within a wider control architecture. 1 Jul 2026 EN · English · Article · AI Advances AI-Native Workflows Have a Moat Problem Where durable differentiation can sit in AI-native workflows. Browse the complete EN / UA archive ↗ 04 / Public discussion & responses How others have engaged with the work. Public recommendations, interpretations and discussion of Uncertainty Architecture. Arkadiy Dobkin Principal Founder & Executive Chairman · EPAM Recommended a full reading of Thinking Systems and extended the argument toward new addressable problems, domain-specific bounding architecture and runtime control. Public record ↗ Maximiliano Armesto Chief Technology Officer · Taller Supported the changed-engineering-object framing, emphasizing boundaries, evidence, authority, correction loops and the return of human judgment. Public record ↗ Markus Kopko Founder · PMotion.ai; CPMAI Lead Coach Connected UA’s control-theory framing with CPMAI practices, roles and governance gates. Public record ↗ Christophe Kolb & Taller Founder & CEO · Taller Cited UA in an explanation of agentic-system control and developed a public visual explanation drawing on it. Public record ↗ Taller’s visual explainer ↗ Michael Risch Senior Project Manager Developed an operational interpretation linking UA to roles, evaluation signals and governance practices. Public record ↗ Matthew Skelton Founder · Conflux; co-author of Team Topologies Offered public encouragement for the research’s development. Public record ↗ Rod Montgomery AI Platform & Developer Acceleration · Corning Hosted the Corning Learn-AI-Palooza discussion and reflected on system-level risks, teams and ownership. Public record ↗ Otman Basir Professor, Electrical & Computer Engineering · University of Waterloo Brought related control-theoretic research into the public discussion of UA. Public record ↗ Related paper ↗ I separately credit Arkadiy Dobkin for the formulation “Thinking Systems”; the provenance note records its scope . Full discussion & source context ↗ 05 / About From quality engineering to delivery leadership. My work has included building delivery functions, resource planning, risk governance and organizational design. It shapes the questions I bring to AI: what teams need to understand, how decisions are made, and who owns the outcome. I write for architects, engineering and delivery leaders, product owners and PMO practitioners. This site connects the publications and living research behind that work. LinkedIn ↗ GitHub ↗ Medium ↗ 06 / Contact Working through one of these problems? Bring a system, a delivery bottleneck, or a question you cannot yet frame. We can discuss where the uncertainty sits and what a useful next step could look like. Research collaboration, speaking invitations and professional opportunities are welcome too. Book a conversation Direct booking will be available here. In the meantime, message me on LinkedIn to arrange a conversation. Research / Living questions Two systems. One engineering perspective. How we deliver software, and how we govern systems whose behavior relies on model judgment — including AI agents in production. Projects Control & constraints Vocabulary Conversations 01 / Research Two directions, connected. 01 How we deliver software The Subprime Code Crisis What happens across review, testing, security and maintenance when generating code gets easier? This research synthesis studies AI-assisted software delivery as a complete system: verification capacity, code quality, technical debt and long-term ownership, with an inspectable evidence library and adaptable operating protocols. Verification capacity System throughput Long-term ownership Explore the research 02 What we build Uncertainty Architecture How do we design and operate software whose behavior depends on probabilistic Model Judgment? Uncertainty Architecture develops an engineering vocabulary and draft specification for Thinking Systems, AI control architecture, evaluation, decision authority, runtime control and correction. Model judgment Control architecture Release & runtime evidence Explore the framework The repositories hold the living research and its sources. My articles connect the ideas across both directions. Two engineering lenses Feedback meets flow. Control theory What do we observe, who can act, and how do we correct behavior? My AI governance writing connects feedback, operating boundaries and corrective action to the design of model-mediated systems. Read the control-theory article ↗ Theory of Constraints (TOC) Where is the bottleneck, and does speeding up one step improve the whole system? The Subprime Code Crisis uses Goldratt’s Theory of Constraints as a lens for verification capacity, work in progress and delivery throughput. Read the delivery-system interpretation ↗ TOC background · TOCICO Research themes AI governance, architecture & operating models. The technical system and the human operating model have to work together. These are the questions behind my writing. Thinking Systems & Model Judgment In UA, Thinking Systems are identified by material runtime responsibilities that depend partly on probabilistic Model Judgment. The category is about an engineering condition, not consciousness or a guarantee of reliability. Judgment Nodes locate where model judgment influences behavior; Uncertainty Boundaries connect deterministic responsibilities with that judgment. Read the current UA vocabulary AI Control Plane & runtime control AI control theory connects boundaries, evidence, decision authority and effective corrective action. UA's AI Control Plane is a distributed capability model across software, evaluation, release decisions and human workflows — not necessarily a central platform. Explore the control capabilities Consequential Runtime Responsibility Which model-mediated outputs, decisions or actions can materially affect outcomes, constraints, authority or downstream people and systems? That question helps connect AI architecture with evaluation, release evidence and accountability. Read the responsibility boundary Socio-technical AI operating models I study the socio-technical stack around AI: how team roles, review practices, decision rights, evaluation and incident ownership fit together. AI governance is not only a model setting; it also concerns how people operate and change the system. It is not claimed to preserve every foreground pixel. No general reuse permission for the photograph is granted here; contact me before using it elsewhere. Language labels The website interface is English. Publication-language labels use EN for English and UA for Ukrainian; machine-readable language codes are en and uk. UA in a project name means Uncertainty Architecture. A platform edition is not automatically a translation; unconfirmed talk languages are labelled explicitly. Display preferences Auto uses your device's local time: Day from 07:00 until 19:00, Night otherwise. You can choose either theme yourself. Motion off freezes both the camera and the structures; your reduced-motion preference overrides a saved On choice. Theme changes only recolor that view.
